channel.title: Prokhorov® — Blog
channel.description: Notes by Artem Prokhorov on web design and development — how websites are planned, designed and built, and what each project teaches along the way.

item.title: Fewer Screens, Clearer Product
item.description: How I redesigned a product dashboard by taking screens away, starting from the views people open every day, and why the new visual style came last.

item.title: Five Questions to Answer Before You Design a Homepage
item.description: Five questions to answer in plain sentences before a homepage is designed, and why the one about a visitor's doubts shapes the page most.

item.title: What a UX Audit Actually Finds
item.description: What I usually find when I review a website's UX: answers in the wrong order, doubts nobody addresses, slow first screens, and how I rank the fixes.

item.title: How I Use AI in Design and Development
item.description: How I use Claude Code to build websites and Figma's AI for routine file work, and why I still draw the final design and write the copy myself.

item.title: Design and Development in One Pair of Hands
item.description: Why I now build the websites I design, what changes when the designer is also the developer, and when a separate development team is the better choice.

item.title: How I Price Fixed-Scope Projects
item.description: How I price website projects: where prices start, what the written scope includes, how payment and timelines work, and what happens when the scope changes.

item.title: One Page or a Full Site
item.description: How I decide whether a project needs a landing page or a multi-page website: what you sell, where visitors come from and how much they need to trust you.

item.title: Structure Before Style
item.description: Why every website I design starts as a sitemap and a plain-text outline of each page, and what that changes for the design and the price.
